14	# Phase 02 Learnings: package-management-sync
15	
16	## Decisions
17	
18	### Per-manager review, no cross-manager coordinator
19	Each package job runs plan → review → apply inside its own `execute()` via an injected reviewer. `PackagePhaseCoordinator` was built, then removed.
20	
21	**Rationale:** A cross-manager review contradicts the job independence D-15 requires. The original reading of "one batched review grouped by manager" as cross-manager was never what the user asked for.
22	**Source:** 02-14-SUMMARY.md, 02-15-SUMMARY.md
23	
24	### Four jobs, not three — `manual_installs_sync` owns unreproducible detection
25	Unreproducible-item detection and the snippet registry moved out of `apt_sync` into their own job with its own enable flag.
26	
27	**Rationale:** Folded into `apt_sync`, disabling apt sync silently disabled manual-install detection; and half the work (unowned files under `/usr/local` and `/opt`) is not apt's business.
28	**Source:** 02-17-SUMMARY.md
29	
30	### Version divergence is asymmetric: apt and flatpak float, snap converges
31	apt and flatpak report a version difference and change nothing; snap converges revision and channel.
32	
33	**Rationale:** Snap stores per-user app data in revision-numbered directories `~/snap/<app>/<rev>/`. apt uses stable paths and flatpak uses id-named `~/.var/app/<id>`, so only snap's data path embeds the version — both machines must sit on the same revision for `folder_sync` to mirror the active data dir.
34	**Source:** 02-UAT-REVIEW-FIXES.md (issue #118)
35	
36	### The snippet registry travels by its own job's `send_file`, never `config_sync`
37	`manual_installs_sync.after_review()` pushes `package-snippets.yaml` itself; `config_sync` carries `config.yaml` only.
38	
39	**Rationale:** `config_sync` runs at SyncStep 9, before any review, so it cannot carry a snippet the user has not authored yet. `folder_sync` cannot be relied on either — user sync jobs are user-controllable, so no job's correctness may depend on another running.
40	**Source:** 02-18-SUMMARY.md
41	
42	### Reproducibility is classified from the source registry, and snippets apply the same run
43	`plan()` reads `SnippetRegistry(self.source)`; `after_review()` pushes the registry, then promotes on-the-fly-authored snippets to INSTALL.
44	
45	**Rationale:** The source is the machine being replicated. Classifying from the target meant a freshly authored snippet was only applied on the *next* run.
46	**Source:** 02-22-SUMMARY.md
47	
48	### A version mismatch is structurally unconvergeable, not merely undecided
49	Mismatches plan as `DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH`/`DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY`, and `apply()` drops every REPORT_ONLY diff regardless of the recorded decision.
50	
51	**Rationale:** A guard that depends on a decision can be defeated by a wrong decision. Excluding the action class outright means no answer can force-converge a mismatch.
52	**Source:** 02-VERIFICATION.md, `packages/sync_core.py:441`
53	
54	### apt collateral is classified auto vs manual before anything is refused
55	Collateral that is auto-installed proceeds silently; manual collateral becomes a three-way install-anyway/skip/abort review item asked at plan time.
56	
57	**Rationale:** Blanket refusal of any install whose `apt-get -s` simulation removes something blocks legitimate installs whose only collateral is a dependency nobody chose.
58	**Source:** 02-16-SUMMARY.md
59	
60	### Shared package helpers live in `jobs/packages/`
61	`items.py`, `review.py`, `state.py`, `sync_core.py` moved into a subpackage with the `package_` prefix stripped; job modules and `base.py`/`context.py` stay in `jobs/` for discovery.
62	
63	**Rationale:** `jobs/` should hold job modules plus the base and context only.
64	**Source:** 02-19-SUMMARY.md
65	
66	### questionary over InquirerPy
67	
68	**Rationale:** The legitimacy gate was cleared by explicit user approval plus live PyPI/GitHub verification (2138 stars, 24 releases 2018–2025, creation date matching first PyPI release) — not training-data recall.
69	**Source:** 02-02-SUMMARY.md
70	
71	### The decision file is machine-local and never synced; the snippet registry is shared
72	`*.decisions.yaml` is excluded from `folder_sync` by a global-first, non-overridable glob that `packages/state.py` owns.
73	
74	**Rationale:** "This package is mine" is a statement about one machine. Syncing it would export one machine's exclusions to the other.
75	**Source:** 02-04-SUMMARY.md
76	
77	### `HELD_OR_PINNED` outranks version-mismatch and removal
78	Any target item named by a hold or pin reports as held/pinned even when its versions also differ.
79	
80	**Rationale:** The hold is the more informative thing to show — it explains why the other difference exists.
81	**Source:** 02-05-SUMMARY.md
82	
83	### Skip-once is a valid resolution, not an unresolved state
84	Only a cancelled or abandoned review leaves an item unresolved and fails the job.
85	
86	**Rationale:** The user may be declining something temporary; that answer should not make the run unclean.
87	**Source:** 02-CONTEXT.md (D-21 corrected), 02-15-SUMMARY.md
88	
89	### snapd auto-refresh is paused via `snap set system refresh.hold`, not `snap refresh --hold`
90	Written on both hosts, with a timed value, restoring the machine's prior policy in cleanup.
91	
92	**Rationale:** `snap refresh --hold` with no snap name sets an *indefinite* global hold and its `--unhold` clears unrelated per-snap holds. The system option is symmetric with the read-only `snap get`, and a timed value self-expires as a crash backstop. Consequence: passwordless sudo is now required on the source too, not just the target.
93	**Source:** 02-UAT-REVIEW-FIXES.md
94	
95	## Lessons
96	
97	### The shared base's `plan()` was apt-shaped, and both later managers had to override it
98	`PackageSyncJob.diff_items()` hardcodes `ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE` and reads `.version`, a field `SnapItem` and `FlatpakItem` do not carry. Both `SnapSyncJob` and `FlatpakSyncJob` override `plan()` entirely, against their plans' literal "inherit `plan()` unchanged" instruction, and reuse only `DecisionFile`/`filter_inert`/`_build_review_groups`.
99	
100	**Context:** The abstraction was extracted from one manager, so it encoded that manager's item shape. Flatpak hit it for a second reason — the base has no notion of one item class that must converge before another (remotes before refs).
101	**Source:** 02-08-SUMMARY.md, 02-09-SUMMARY.md
102	
103	### Faithful execution of a wrong decision still produces the wrong system
104	Plans 02-01 to 02-13 shipped, were code-reviewed and went green in CI, then 02-14 to 02-21 removed the coordinator, split out a fourth job and reverted `config_sync`. Nothing was defective; the decisions were.
105	
106	**Context:** The rework was caught only by a human reading the executed phase. The correction was made as a delta replan in place rather than a new phase, because nothing had merged yet.
107	**Source:** 02-14-SUMMARY.md through 02-21-SUMMARY.md
108	
109	### Only the real VM run found the same-run defect
110	`manual_installs_sync` applied source-authored snippets one run too late. Twenty-one plans of unit tests, review and type-checking did not surface it; the first CI integration run on PR #206 did.
111	
112	**Context:** The unit tests seeded the registry wherever the code read it, so they agreed with the bug. Only an end-to-end run over two machines could disagree.
113	**Source:** 02-21-SUMMARY.md, 02-22-SUMMARY.md
114	
115	### A grep acceptance criterion can contradict the prose of its own plan
116	Three times: `manager_name: ClassVar` contains the substring `name: ClassVar` the same plan required absent; a docstring explaining `grep -c 'review_items' == 0` was itself a match; a correctly negated sentence ("no coordinator sits between the jobs") failed `grep -ci 'coordinator' == 0`.
117
